text: On the wind-scoured Hadrow Flats, where the salt pan has long shimmered like a broken mirror, survey crews from the private Kestrel Bore Consortium confirmed this week what local geologists had suspected for months: a substantial lithium brine deposit lies beneath the crust. The finding follows a 14-month drilling program begun after a 2024 magnetotelluric scan hinted at unusually conductive layers below the basin floor. Lead surveyor Mara Elling said the brine samples averaged 1,420 milligrams of lithium per litre across three test wells, a figure deemed commercially significant. For the surrounding district, long dependent on grazing and seasonal salt scraping, the discovery recalls older booms that arrived with promises of renewal and left only dust, roads, and memory.
